newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines arrests leftist anti-APEC leader.
newsitem.headline: Philippines arrests leftist anti-APEC leader.

text.p: Philippine soldiers on Tuesday arrested one of the country's top leftist leaders in what his supporters said was a move to neutralise opponents of this month's APEC summit.
An army spokesman confirmed the arrest of Filemon Lagman but said he was taken into custody in connection with the killing of a policeman in 1992.

Military intelligence reports have linked Lagman's group to plans to disrupt the November 25 summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum to be attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton and leaders of 17 other member economies.

Manila newspapers have reported that these plans include fomenting unrest among workers in the hotel, transport and telecommunications sectors, which all provide key support services to the APEC summit.
Lagman is chairman of the leftist BMP (Coalition of Filipino Workers) which is organising an anti-APEC workers' meeting coinciding with the summit.
"The military wants to neutralise him for the APEC (summit) ... and deliver a strong signal to all other anti-APEC groups," BMP spokesman Wilson Fortaleza told Reuters.
